sources.title: University of Vienna: The Rutbils of Zabulistan and the Emperor of Rome
sources.note: Direct full text checked. Uses independence after 680, royal geography, Tang investitures, multilingual coinage and uncertain eras. Does not adopt its misleading description of Yaqub as Arab or its oversimplified 870 final ending.

sources.title: Hyecho: Memoirs of a Pilgrimage, in Collected Works of Korean Buddhism 10 (2012)
sources.note: Direct complete PDF checked. Roderick Whitfield ed.; Matty Wegehaupt, Michael Finch and Sem Vermeersch translators. Printed pp.136 to 140 (PDF165 to 169) and 152 (PDF181). Treats traveler generalizations as attributed reports. All derived words across the volume grouped.

sources.title: Italian Archaeological Mission: The Buddhist site of Tapa Sardar
sources.note: Direct full institutional excavation synthesis. General features; recent period; restoration. Pottery catalogue below conservatively grouped with this work in cumulative budget. Distinct from existing Ghaznavid-palace dossier.

sources.title: Italian Archaeological Mission: Tapa Sardar pottery TS01003
sources.note: Indexed original complete record checked; direct page timed out. Exact query site:ghazni.bdus.cloud/buddhist/finds/pottery goats returns TS01003. II terrace, Passage34 (2), wheel-turned stamped red clay, late period, maximum9.1cm, two running goats.

sources.title: Natasha N. Kimmet: Red Clay-based Buddhist Sculpture in the Shahi Kingdoms (2022)
sources.note: Direct full PDF, printed p.7/PDF6 Tapa Sardar section and footnote24. Do not borrow neighboring Fondukistan, Qol-i Tut or Mes Aynak details. Durga TS1145 approximately64cm, seventh/eighth-century production.

sources.title: Giulia Forgione: Gemstones as Pure Symbols, Tapa Sardar (2024)
sources.note: Institutional author repository abstract checked, matching publisher DOI10.1163/24685631-12340151. Abstract only; entire article paywalled. Only abstract-supported decoration and interpretation used.

sources.title: J. Harmatta and B. A. Litvinsky: Tokharistan and Gandhara under Western Turk Rule (1996)
sources.note: UNESCO History of Civilizations of Central Asia III, chapter16, The fight for independence, coin paragraph beginning The legend of his coins runs as follows. Exact indexed original verified via queries šrī vākhudevah His Highness and site:almuslih.org Zabulistan Brahmi. PDF direct extraction failed, so no invented page number. Transcription and translation exact. Older Jibul identification and precise735 conversion not adopted because Vienna catalogue stresses uncertain names and eras. Original Brahmi glyphs not reconstructed.

sources.title: Erdoğan Merçil: Saffar, Yaqub ibn Layth, TDV Islam Ansiklopedisi (2008)
sources.note: Direct full article, print vol35 pp.463 to 464. Paragraphs beginning Büst şehrine and Ya‘kūb Fars’ta: 864 Zunbil death, Firuz regained Zabulistan, Yaqub869 expedition and873 capture. Compared Bosworth Iranica Yaqub and Saffarids entries; published dates differ, so public account uses864 to 865 and later860s/early870s. No source reuse found.

proposedOverrides.summary: Zabulistan’s frontier rulers joined diplomacy and multilingual coinage with a rich Buddhist artistic landscape.

batchIdentityNotes.note: Exact imported700 to 800 record, one decodedworld-700 polygon. Bbox64.420844,30.550763,68.701287,34.110635. Point tests includeKandahar/Zamindawar nearMusaQala but excludeGhazni,Bost,Kabul; public caveat explicit. Narrative centers eighth-centuryZabul with clearly marked earlier/later context. Noalias to HinduShahis, Kabul, Umayyads, Abbasids or Saffarids. TapaSardar chronology and royal patronage do not prove exact ethnic affiliation. Hyecho comparative clothing/products and broad family report explicitly attributed, not universalized. No attested school, hospital or toilet plan established for this record; no invented details. Coin sample remains verified scholarly transliteration, not recreated original glyphs. Religion cannot be reduced to one label. Ending uses staged Saffarid conquest with Firuz recovery and873capture rather than catalog shortcut870. No successor links invented because actual event year lacks matching importedSaffarid snapshot.
